Diego,

Jared —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a recommended path:

1) Itemized SKU-level metering on invoice: yes. We can surface per-SKU usage lines on the marketplace invoice if you select SKU-by-SKU reporting in the private offer. That requires us to map the internal SKU codes to the marketplace SKUs during onboarding.

2) Reseller uplift evidence: we typically need (a) the reseller agreement (signed) showing margin terms, and (b) an invoice routing manifest that tells us which invoice lines should be passed through. In many cases customers also opt to receive a monthly reconciliation CSV we generate that includes per-SKU usage and net-back calculations for the reseller.

3) Blended SKU price approach: two common options — (a) publish an explicit blended SKU in the private offer (recommended if you want a single line on your internal chargeback), or (b) send market-itemized SKUs and let your internal billing system apply a blended view. Option (a) is cleaner for procurement but loses per-SKU visibility unless we also emit a reconciliation file.

Recommended path for CloudSentry (given your reseller requirement):
- We create itemized SKUs on the offer so the reseller gets per-SKU lines.
- We also deliver a monthly reconciliation CSV (sample attached) that includes per-SKU list price, applied discount, reseller uplift percent and net-back calculations.
- You provide signed reseller agreement + invoice routing manifest.

I've attached a draft mapping workbook (redwood-uplift-workbook.xlsx) and a small SKU export template (gcp-sku-list.csv) — can you confirm those formats map to your internal systems?

If that sounds good I can loop in Irene (billing & marketplace ops) and Ben (channel ops) to tighten the evidence checklist and confirm tax/invoice routing details. Would you prefer a quick 30-min call or shall we handle via email?

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Diego / all —

Quick updates after verifying with Marketplace Ops & Finance:

1) SKU-level invoice lines: Confirmed. For GCP private offers we can surface per-SKU lines if the private offer is configured with SKU itemization. Caveats: (a) workload-derived dynamic SKUs (e.g., ephemeral burst nodes) require a mapping step — we will ask CloudSentry to supply a usage sample (their CSV) to map rows to marketplace SKU ids.

2) Reconciliation CSV: We can include these fields: date range, marketplace_sku_id, customer_usage_units, list_price_per_unit, applied_discount, reseller_uplift_percent, reseller_netback. Ben and I will standardize the netback calc (list_price * usage * (1 - discount) * (1 - reseller_uplift_percent)). We will include a sample file.

3) Reseller evidence: For US-reseller pass-through we require: signed reseller agreement (PDF), invoice routing manifest with reseller remit-to and tax id, and reseller W-9 (or local equivalent). For EU resellers, VAT registration must be provided.

4) Tax treatment: Laura confirmed uplift shown as a pass-through line; Redwood will not recognize the uplift as revenue if we are forwarding it to the reseller on the invoice (it flows through). We still need the reseller tax docs on file for accounting.

Next steps for Diego / Jared: please send a 7–14 day sample usage CSV (anonymized) to irene_choi@redwood.com so we can validate mapping. Ben and I will produce the reconciliation template and a short runbook for procurement evidence. Once those are accepted we can proceed to create a draft private offer in the GCP console.

Jared — happy to hop on a 30-min call Wed/Thu (I put some slots in a shared calendar invite). If you prefer email, please send the sample CSV.

Thanks —
Irene Choi
Marketplace Operations — Redwood Inference
